unit: Obed resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Seeking to hire a young boy from an asylum to help with farm work in his old age, he traveled to Alder River only to find that an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake. Unable to break the news to her, he brought her home and quietly insisted on keeping her, quickly forming a warm, affectionate bond with her. Over the next four years, he took immense pride in Nell's academic success and achievements, encouraging her ambitions and defending her against harsh judgments. His health gradually declined due to worsening heart spells, and he was forbidden from performing heavy farm labor. Shortly after Nell won the Avery scholarship, Obed passed away peacefully, leaving behind a lasting legacy of love and gratitude in Nell's heart.

unit: Rosalind Penrose grew up in Welby, named by her father after his love for lavender sheets during his courtship of her mother. In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became betrothed to Stephen Stanhope, but the engagement suddenly ended following a disagreement, prompting Stanhope to leave for the United States. After her mother died a decade prior, Rosalind withdrew into Echo Cottage—an ancient stone house built by her English grandfather—and effectively faded from local social life. Unable to afford an adult servant, she arranged for a succession of young handmaidens from the Bowman family to live with her; because of their similar appearances, she called each of them "Belinda" in turn up through Belinda the Fourth. She later formed a close friendship with schoolmistress Nell Harcourt, frequently hosting her for tea, confectionery making, and pretend parties. Eventually, Stephen Stanhope returned, rekindled their romance, and escorted her on forest walks. They were married in an unceremonious service in the honeysuckle garden at Echo Cottage, officiated by Mr. Wace.

label: History
value: Following the sudden death of Obed, Nell remained at Grey Shutters to support Thirza.
unit: Nell Harcourt was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia, to high school teachers Edmund and Bertha Harcourt, both of whom died of fever shortly after her birth. She was taken in by Mrs. Thomas until age eight, then moved upriver to care for Mrs. Rudge's children, and eventually ended up in an asylum at Marden for four months. She was brought from the asylum to Brierley to reside at Grey Shutters with Thirza Abernethy and Obed Abernethy, who became her guardians and loved her like their own child. Nell attended the local school, engaging in a intense academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow. She later pursued Second Year work at Regent's Academy, earning high honors and winning the Avery scholarship. Following the sudden death of Obed, Nell remained at Grey Shutters to support Thirza, took up a job as a local schoolteacher, and served as secretary for the newly founded Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, she prepared to leave Brierley to attend Wexcombe College alongside Hugh.
